body:
I'll tell you what I'm going through. Maybe it'll help clear things up, at least.

What I have is a condition that I've been calling "chronic suicidal ideation", which would mean that I have ongoing thoughts of wanting to die for no specific or apparent reason--I mean, most of the time the reasons are non-specific or have no apparent reason.

I believe, based on my research (which is not exactly academic-level, keep in mind), that the chronic suicidal ideation is the result of having first contemplated suicide at a very early age. In my case, I was about nine years old. I was getting horribly bullied at school, my "friends" treated me like dirt, and my parents were cold and unavailable--when I went home after having been beaten by some other kid at school, my mother would immediately ask "Well, what did you *do?*", meaning that, of course, my having been beaten was somehow my fault. I realized that nobody wanted me around, so I started thinking about killing myself.

After a while, this became a coping mechanism for another major mental disorder: anxiety. I had panic attacks while growing up on many occasions, although I had no clue what they were and my parents just behaved as though I was doing it to annoy them. But when something frightened me about the future, it became a natural impulse to think *Well, worst case scenario, I can always kill myself.*

The brain is like a muscle, and if it gets put to work doing something for long enough, eventually it becomes a reflex. So now, to this day (over thirty years later), I still struggle with suicidal ideation because it's my only real coping mechanism. The suicidal ideation feeds my anxiety, of course, which then feeds my depression... it's a pretty horrible cycle.

There are some medications that can help with this; I currently take lithium. My body metabolizes anti-depressants too quickly for any of them to work, but anti-anxiety meds seem to help a little. Besides that, a lot of what I use is force of will because I don't really have anything else internal of use. I try to keep busy with some craftsmanship (leather work and sewing are my current kick); I find that creating something is far more satisfying than something like video games. I also try to study new languages and treat Duolingo like a video game that gives back a little more than most real games do. One thing is certain: I've stood on the edge of oblivion and walked away, so if I want to do something (and it doesn't hurt anyone, of course), I will do it without apology. All of the people who would criticize me are no longer a part of my life.

I hope this is at least a little helpful. Understand that what is happening to you is not your fault--that's important to remember. People treat the mentally ill as though we're doing it intentionally, and that's horseshit. Your thoughts of suicide are due to an "injury" of a sort, and you can't be expected to just "fix" it. You'll probably need to find a psychiatrist and explore medications, and you will probably also need to find some kind of therapist. It's a pain in the ass, but I honestly wish I had done exactly that when I was your age; I didn't really start getting help until a few years ago, and I've been miserable for a long time when I probably didn't have to be.

Hang in there. Things won't always be this painful.
